title: 2026 U.S. Senate election in Maine
description: Maine will elect one U.S. senator in 2026 for the Class II seat currently held by Republican Susan Collins. The race is closely watched because Collins is a long-serving incumbent in a state that often votes competitively in federal elections. Democrats are trying to flip the seat, and the contest has featured a contrast between Collins and Democratic challengers Graham Platner and Janet Mills. The primary is scheduled for June 9, 2026, with the general election on November 3, 2026.

flags.concern: Andrea LaFlamme's Tech & AI stance shows medium confidence but cites only environmental priorities (banning data centers) rather than substantive AI policy positions. The stance description conflates data-center restrictions with AI governance, which are related but distinct issues.
flags.suggestion: Either clarify that the 'Tech & AI' position is primarily about data-center energy/environmental concerns rather than AI-specific governance, or lower confidence further and note that a comprehensive AI policy position was not found.

flags.concern: Susan Collins' abortion stance is marked 'medium' confidence, which is appropriate given the nuance. However, the sourcing includes a Planned Parenthood action fund statement framing her votes negatively ('votes to raise health care costs and restrict abortion access'). While this is a legitimate source, it presents one advocacy organization's interpretation rather than neutral reporting. The stance description itself is balanced ('generally described herself as supporting abortion rights with some restrictions'), but the second source is an advocacy claim rather than neutral reporting of her position.
flags.suggestion: Consider adding a neutral reporting source (e.g., nonpartisan vote analysis or her own campaign statement on abortion) to balance the advocacy-framed source, or note explicitly that the Planned Parenthood characterization is advocacy commentary rather than factual reporting of her votes.

flags.concern: Susan Collins' Civil Rights stance focuses narrowly on transgender student protections and uses news reporting of her actions (backing a referendum) as the primary source. The description characterizes her positions via news headlines rather than her own public statements. While not inaccurate, this creates an asymmetry: Democratic candidates' stances are sourced to their own campaign platforms, while Collins' stance is sourced to news coverage of her opposition to a policy. This is not bias in the profile itself, but it reflects the structural reality that Republican candidates' positions are sometimes documented primarily through news reporting of their actions rather than affirmative policy statements.
flags.suggestion: If available, supplement with a statement from Collins or her campaign articulating her own framing of the transgender student policy position, to provide parity with how Democratic candidates' stances are sourced.

flags.concern: Janet Mills' career history shows end_year of 2027 for Governor, but the profile is dated May 17, 2026, and Mills' governorship began in 2019. Maine governors serve 4-year terms; if Mills began in 2019, her term would end in 2023 or 2027 depending on whether she won reelection in 2022. The end_year of 2027 implies she is still serving or will serve through early 2027, which is consistent with a two-term governor elected in 2022. However, no source explicitly confirms her current status or whether she is still serving. This is a minor dating issue but should be verified.
flags.suggestion: Confirm via an official Maine government source that Mills' governorship extends through 2027 (i.e., she was reelected in 2022 and is currently serving), or adjust the end_year if she has already left office.

flags.concern: David Costello's donor summary references an FEC page for a 2001–2002 House run ('the 2001–2002 FEC page for a prior House run'), which appears to be a prior candidacy. The profile notes that his current 2026 Senate FEC page 'was not fully extractable in the available text.' The citation mixes data from a historical run with inability to extract current-cycle data. While this is transparently documented, it creates ambiguity about the actual current fundraising profile.
flags.suggestion: Clarify in donor_summary that the $69.1K figure is from a prior (2001–2002) House run, not the current 2026 Senate cycle, and note that current-cycle totals could not be fully extracted from available FEC pages. Recommend human reviewer check FEC directly for 2026 cycle.

flags.concern: The polling section includes a UNH Survey Center poll (Feb. 16, 2026) and an Emerson poll (April 7, 2026) with null percentages for all candidates, and notes state 'some source pages in search results did not expose full toplines in accessible text.' This is transparently acknowledged, but it raises the question of data completeness. The RealClearPolling entry provides actual percentages (Platner 47.3%, Collins 40.5%), but two of three polls are incomplete.
flags.suggestion: Human reviewer should visit the UNH (https://scholars.unh.edu/survey_center_polls/930/) and Emerson (https://emersoncollegepolling.com/maine-2026-poll-platner-leads-gov-mills-democrats-lead-sen-collins-in-maine/) URLs directly to extract missing toplines if available; note in polling_note that human verification of these specific URLs is recommended.

reviews.summary: This profile demonstrates strong overall sourcing and internal consistency across all five candidates.
